notes.title: Patch 0.77 - The new beginning
notes.notes:
After the last games awarded for it's game design and success, we decided to change the game direction through a new goal: Fida Puti Samurai will be a shooter no more - but a mere virtual place to play another game: Dog Duty Survivor. The development efforts will be driven entirely to this new game-inside-of-this-game, and the fps mechanics will be changed entirely.

On the next updates, the enemies will not drop money, but instead, materials, like material_a, material_b, material_c and so on (our narrative department will develop pseudo-meaningful names for those materials later on). You may also get those materials by purchasing it on our new store OR acquired by subscribing to a battle pass plan, that will also grant skins that you will use to watch yourself on a mirror alone.

Since console players do not buy games anymore after gamepass, we will need to get rid of all nasty content, and replace it with cute dogs and cats. The in-game characters will use heavy armor covering all the troublesome bits (Gamepass may enjoy adding Cyberpunk 2077 to it's "desirables" list but a unknow nsfw indie shooter? nah!).

On this patch, some things slipped, and will be removed later:
-Fox Legs are now purchaseable AND both arms and legs gives +7 armor, with no ammo bonus.
-DVD animations are now de-censored. I've also replaced some animations, changed others. Those new animations will be semi-nsfw, and safer ones will play if playing on "SFW mode" (but I need to double check it!)
-Other little things here and there.

Next patch will include the new game $tore and the battlepass subscriptions. Stay tuned!

notes.title: New goals for Early Access (also, patch notes for v0.5)
notes.notes:
Hi there! We're reaching the final date of the Early Access conclusion, that was set on March 21 of 2021. From that point, the promise was to deliver the full game on June 30, that is, Friday next week, with 3 episodes, each containing 4 levels, with the possibility of core gameplay changes along the way.

A lot of things happened during this time frame. We participated on Realms Deep 2021. For our absolute surprise, Civvie11 picked the game to play. I've met absolutely great players that helped the game with insightful and really important feedback. And I moved from house 2 times, looking for a quieter place to work on the game (unfortunately, this place was not found yet).

With the support of the community, the game/project endured LOTS of drawbacks, and I had the opportunity to keep working on the project, and got the energy to stay strong while doing it. The game got it's 3 episodes, it's levels, new enemies, mechanics. Shaped the game lore. Solved difficult bugs (most famous, the no-hit/agression bug, that was a Unity3d Physics bug) among other things. And by last, I learned a lot with the experience.

So, whats next: there's lots of things that I still want to work, in order to deliver a full game. Among those things:

-I want to finish the last concluding chapter of the game
-Solve bugs that are still in the game
-Polish the game levels (I want to give more personality the levels as overall)
-Add new weapons, and polish some of the existing ones.
-There's enemies lacking unique voices
-I still want to add more variety to the in-game city, and add new stores. And new silly dvds with silly videos to play
-Last but very important - I want to improve the experience of playing/living inside the main cabin, the hub-house. I want to add new shop tabs, more content to purchase, and more options for turning the cabin into a good place to chill out.

I'm a little afraid of setting deadlines, but I want to do it all for December of this year. I want to finish the Early Access package and, if there's more ideas, I will separate for a sequel-or-dlc-or-patch, just to help me focus on delivering a completed project.

Once again, I'm very very thankful for everyone who supported the game, gave feedback and all. It helped me endure on the darkest of times.

notes.title: Update notes for May 30

This one took a little more time, on a fundamental ingame change that I needed to approach.

But why? Two things: first, since the game does not lock you on finding colored keys or activating things, I was looking into ways of giving meaning to the game combat, to... you know, avoid the game being an entire speedrun only thing.
Another issue was the Rogue-Lite elements. Until now, the way to save things on your house stash was to drop any weapon-or-item on a mailbox, then this item would be saved on your cabin/hub. I personally like when there's not-so-obvious design ideas on game (Dog Duty is totally based on that) but... I think that the mail box alone was not doing it's job, and also, imposing some limitations.

So... how to solve those 2 questions? Well... since Liza LOVES to browse stuff on e-shops (I dont see reason on that, but that's her thing) I'm changing the game system to work with currency, and adding some e-shops on the cabin's computer. So now.... you may win currency by killing enemies, and you may use it to buy permanent upgrades, house decor, and weapons, on the confort of your basement's computer.

But beware, dying ingame makes you lose 95% of your currency - you will be able to keep it by:
a - depositing the value on mailboxes
b - ending the episode

What do you think? That makes sense?
Also, on this patch, other things:
